body: [P2] `.github/scripts/ci_shadow_pair.py:131` permits identical accepted/candidate invocations even when the candidate behavioral order is narrower. On the current head, using `tests.test_ci_shadow_pair.example(False)` (accepted B=[A,B], candidate B=[A]), setting `candidate['driver']['invocation'] = accepted['driver']['invocation'][:]` makes both commands `python experiment.py --role accepted`; `compare_pair` nevertheless returns `pair_status='observed-matching-pair'` with `blockers=[]`. The existing role-only test even asserts this result. Thus the 2B paired-observation status can claim a matching candidate run without an invocation that selects the candidate path. Please mark changed-order pairs inconclusive unless the driver identity distinguishes the accepted/candidate roles (or bind an equivalent reviewed selection input), and add this counterexample as a negative regression. `activation.eligible=false` is preserved, but it does not correct this PR's own pair-status conclusion. The 11 local comparator tests and current head-bound CI passed; the finding is outside their present acceptance assertion.
